pillars.label: Learning Architecture
pillars.headline: I can structure the learning before I ever open an authoring tool.
pillars.proof: I use the models as decision tools, not ceremony. The pattern is audience → performance need → objective → practice → evidence → delivery constraints.

pillars.label: Enterprise Learning Tech
pillars.headline: I understand the systems around the course, not just the course itself.
pillars.proof: I can translate between the learner experience and the technical owners responsible for identity, enrollment, CRM, reporting, and downstream data.

pillars.label: Accessible UX/UI
pillars.headline: I treat accessibility and usability as interaction design, not a final checklist.
pillars.proof: I design for clear navigation, low cognitive friction, multiple ways to access information, and custom interactions that still work with keyboard and assistive technology.

pillars.label: AI + Automation
pillars.headline: I use AI and code to extend the ID workflow instead of replacing the ID judgment.
pillars.proof: I build constrained, reviewable systems: the model or script gets a defined job, inputs, boundaries, and QA rather than unlimited freedom.

pillars.label: Performance Consulting
pillars.headline: I am comfortable saying training is not the answer when the root cause is somewhere else.
pillars.proof: I look for knowledge, process, access, ownership, documentation, incentive, and system problems before recommending a course. I am continuing formal HPI development and certification work.

pillars.label: Delivery + Collaboration
pillars.headline: I can keep a complex learning project moving without turning review into chaos.
pillars.proof: I separate decisions, dependencies, factual approval, design review, QA, and launch requirements so people know what they own and what needs to happen next.
